summary: The paper investigates Mamba's in-context learning ability on random Markov chains and shows, both empirically and via a constructive proof, that a single-layer Mamba (specifically a simplified 'MambaZero' variant) can exactly represent the Bayes/minimax-optimal Laplacian smoothing estimator for first-order finite-state Markov processes, with convolution identified as the crucial architectural component. A complementary lower bound establishes that any recurrent architecture needs hidden dimension × precision scaling like 2^k to represent the estimator for kth-order chains. The contribution is a genuine and clean addition to the theoretical understanding of SSMs, though the formal theorem is restricted to first-order chains and the beyond-Markov / language-modeling evidence is comparatively thin.
strengths: First careful application of the Markov-ICL framework to Mamba/SSMs, connecting the architecture to a classical optimal estimator (Laplacian / add-β smoothing) rather than to transformer analogs.

Constructive proof (Thm. 1) with explicit parameter choices; the construction is motivated by, and consistent with, learned parameters (a_t≈1, orthogonality/vanishing b·c off the current token), which makes the theory feel mechanistic rather than post-hoc.
Sharp isolation of convolution as the critical ingredient via a clean 3-way ablation (full Mamba, no-conv Mamba, MambaZero) and the w ≥ k+1 relation between convolution window and Markov order.
Complementary lower bound (Thm. 2) that applies to any recurrent architecture at any depth with finite precision, giving a real representational separation intuition vs. transformers.
The switching-Markov experiment is a nice targeted probe showing a_t behaves as a learned reset gate, giving semantic content to the selectivity mechanism beyond the pure Markov setting.

key_concerns.issue: Theorem 1 covers only first-order Markov chains under MambaZero (an L1-normalized, ReLU/gate-stripped simplification), yet the paper repeatedly frames the result as 'Mamba learns the Laplacian estimator for all Markov orders.' Higher-order behavior is asserted only via Fig. 1b, and the transfer from MambaZero to full Mamba is empirical rather than proven.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either extend the construction (or state a formal impossibility/approximation result) for k>1 and for the full Mamba (softmax head, ReLU, gating), or explicitly narrow the abstract/introduction claims to 'first-order, MambaZero'. Add a remark quantifying the gap between MambaZero and full Mamba.

key_concerns.issue: The 'convolution is fundamental' claim generalizes poorly outside the Markov toy setup: on WikiText-103 the convolution effect is only 11% (Mamba) / 2% (Transformer) and, per the authors' own note, shrinks further with depth. This weakens the sweeping claim that convolution is the key mechanism.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Reframe the language-modeling section as 'convolution is helpful, particularly at shallow depth' rather than as evidence that the Markov-derived insight transfers. Report per-seed variance for Table 1 to establish that the 2% transformer gap is even significant.

key_concerns.issue: Experimental breadth is narrow: most sharpness plots are on binary or very small state spaces, single/few-layer models, and 5 seeds. There is no scan over β, no comparison to other SSM variants (S4, S5, LRU, RWKV, xLSTM) despite the related-work section citing them, and no fair Mamba-2 vs. Mamba-1 controls.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add (i) results across a range of state-space sizes S with the theoretical d=2S check, (ii) at least one linear-RNN / S4-style baseline to test whether the Laplacian recovery is specifically a Mamba property or a generic linear-recurrence-with-conv property, and (iii) a β sweep verifying the add-β form (not just add-1).

key_concerns.issue: Statistical reporting is uneven: Fig. 1b has std over 5 runs, but Table 1 and several ablations have no reported variance or significance test, making 2%–11% claims hard to evaluate.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean±std (or CI) over multiple seeds for every headline number, and mark which improvements are statistically significant.

key_concerns.issue: Positioning against Rajaraman et al. (2024) and Sanford et al. (2024)/Ekbote et al. (2025) is asserted but not carefully compared: the claim that Mamba needs d·p ≳ 2^k while transformers need d ≳ k with 3 layers is a strong architectural separation that deserves a dedicated subsection.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a table or short section formally stating the assumptions of each prior bound and making the separation explicit; discuss whether the depth-1 Mamba result is really 'better' when accounting for hidden-dimension cost.

key_concerns.issue: The construction relies on empirically observed properties (a_t≈1, b(ij)·c_t ≈ 0 for i≠x_t, β·1 residual) that are asserted to happen at convergence but are not tied to any optimization guarantee, so the paper elides the gap between 'representable' and 'learned'.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: State clearly that Thm. 1 is a representation result, and provide a numeric check (over many seeds/settings) of how tightly the trained parameters match the theoretical construction (parameter recovery error, not just loss).

key_concerns.issue: Some notation in Sec. 2.2 is garbled in the extraction (e.g., the Input-selectivity block, Δ_t vs t_softplus, ordering of update equations), and Thm. 2's condition 'sufficiently large t' is not quantified.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Clean the Mamba equations block for readability and give an explicit t*(k, ε) in Thm. 2.

questions_for_authors: Can the construction in Thm. 1 be extended to k>1 within MambaZero, and does it require d to grow as S^k, consistent with Thm. 2?
How tight is Thm. 2 for Mamba specifically? The bound is for any recurrent model — is there a matching upper bound showing Mamba achieves ~2^k, or could a smaller SSM class also achieve it?
Does the Laplacian-recovery behavior persist for larger S (e.g., 32, 128) and for β ≠ 1? A β sweep would directly test whether the model learns add-β rather than merely a smooth-count predictor.
In the switching-Markov experiment, is the a_t→0 at switch tokens a learned behavior for all seeds, and how sharply does it generalize to unseen p_switch values?
For the WikiText-103 result, are the 27.55 vs 30.68 perplexities statistically significant across seeds, and does the effect vanish at, say, 6+ layers?

Does replacing the convolution with an equivalent-depth linear MLP over the last w tokens recover the Laplacian estimator? This would clarify whether it is the convolution specifically or any local-context mixer that matters.

How does linear attention (mentioned briefly around Fig. 7) fit into the picture — does it also match the Laplacian estimator with a single layer, and if so, what does that imply for the 'convolution is the key' narrative?
calibration_check: The construction and lower bound are appropriately scoped, but the abstract/intro overreach beyond the first-order MambaZero setting and generalize the 'convolution is the key' finding to language modeling on the strength of a modest 11%/2% perplexity ablation.

significance.justification: A clean and useful contribution to the mechanistic understanding of Mamba/SSMs that the ICL-theory community will likely cite, but not paradigm-shifting: it fills in a first-order corner of a framework already established for transformers.

novelty.justification: First application of the Markov-ICL framework to Mamba and the first explicit Mamba↔Laplacian-smoothing connection with a constructive proof; the framework itself is adapted from Edelman et al. rather than newly invented.

rigor.justification: Thm. 1's construction is careful and matches empirical parameter structure; however, it applies only to MambaZero at k=1, and the extension to full Mamba and higher orders is empirical only.

statistical_soundness.justification: 5-seed error bars for the main sharpness plot, but variance is not reported for the language-modeling table or several ablations, making small effect sizes (2–11%) hard to evaluate.

calibration_honesty.justification: The paper acknowledges that Thm. 1 is representational and that learning dynamics are out of scope, but the abstract/introduction generalize beyond first-order MambaZero and generalize the convolution finding to language modeling on relatively weak evidence.

clarity.justification: The narrative is well organized and the proof sketch is genuinely illuminating; the Mamba-equation block and some notation are dense and would benefit from cleanup.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard conference structure — Introduction, Related Work, Setup, Theory, Experiments beyond Markov, Conclusion — with appendix references for full proofs.

reproducibility.justification: Data generation, loss, optimizer, and architecture are described precisely enough to be reproduced, with hyperparameter details deferred to appendices; the switching-process specifics and Table 1 setup are somewhat under-described in the main text.

related_work.justification: Covers the main SSM/Mamba and Markov-ICL/induction-head lines; positioning vs. Rajaraman/Sanford is asserted rather than carefully compared, and no discussion of other linear-RNN baselines that could isolate Mamba-specific effects.

figure_quality.justification: From the captions, figures directly support the claims (sharpness of the estimator, ablation of convolution, w vs k, learned a_t at switches) and are load-bearing rather than decorative.

breadth_generality.justification: Empirics are dominated by small state spaces, shallow models, and a single language-modeling table; no comparison to other SSM variants and limited β/S/depth sweeps, weakening the 'general finding' framing.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline accept: a mechanistically satisfying but scope-limited theory paper; the core representation and lower-bound results are solid, but breadth of experiments and scope of the main theorem hold it back from a clear accept.
